newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Argentaria profit plunges, recovery seen.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Argentaria profit plunges, recovery seen.

text.p: Spain's Corporacion Bancaria de Espana (Argentaria) on Friday reported profits more than halved in 1996 but it still raised its dividend in a gesture that analysts said suggested a recovery ahead.

Net attributable profit at Argentaria fell 58 percent in 1996 to 31.22 billion pesetas ($227.4 million), in line with expectations of a sharp drop in results. But it confirmed that it would raise its dividend to a gross 277 pesetas from 270 on 1995 earnings.

Argentaria, formed in 1991 in a merger of six state-owned banks and savings banks, has struggled to reduce a mountain of low-yielding assets, expensive liabilities and to cope with a uncompetitively small domestic network.

To help address the pressing problems, Argentaria said in December that it would devote nearly half its 1996 pre-tax profits to reduce the average interest rates on its expensive liabilities and to shore up its balance sheet.
Without the extraordinary charge, pre-tax profit would have been some 43 billion pesetas higher than the 42 billion reported. In 1995, pre-tax profit was 85 billion pesetas.
Chairman Francisco Gonzalez said the decision to devote 43 billion pesetas to save on financial costs would allow "gains in net interest income and in the dividend in coming years."

In other moves, the group raised its stake by 2.12 percent to 5.21 percent in Telefonica de Espana and upped its holding in utility Endesa. It also formed Gesinar to group and reduce the size of its foreclosed real estate holdings.
Banking analysts called the results weak, if unsurprising, although there were signs of a recovery.
"The results are within expectations. They are weak from the operating point of view," said Ignacio Cornejo, analyst at Beta Capital in Madrid.
Operating profit rose just slightly to 89.58 billion pesetas from 82.32 billion pesetas in 1995.
In addition, the bank lost further market share as it tried to reduce the number of assets in search of higher quality.
"Argentaria has lost market share but it has had a policy of reducing volumes to gain profitability," said Juan Cueto, analyst at Ibersecurities.

Last month, Morgan Stanley analyst Jennifer Oliver Martin upgraded her rating on the share to a strong buy with a medium-term share price objective of 7,500. On Friday she said Argentaria's results had reinforced her optimistic views.
Argentaria shares closed down 40 pesetas, or 0.69 percent, at 5,770, outpacing the overall market. The IBEX-35 index fell 126.06 points, or 2.31 percent, to 5,324.68.
"My feelings are definitely the same or even stronger. One can see the benefit of the restructuring," Martin said, pointing to an improvement in traditional banking deposit and loan business.
"And they sent a strong signal by increasing the dividend."
A dealer at a foreign brokerage also said the share could climb after its poor performance recently. Argentaria shares gained just 16 percent last year while the market rose nearly 40 percent.
The bulk of the benefits are not expected to show through until the last half of 1997, Martin said.
